venue.name: Tofino Sea Kayaking
venue.description: Tofino Sea Kayaking runs guided sea kayak day tours that launch from its own waterfront beach at 320 Main Street in downtown Tofino, next to the Coast Guard station. Four day tours are published, from a 2.5 hour paddle around the harbour islands to a 5 hour trip into the inlets of Meares Island, and any of them can also be booked as a private tour. Public day tours have a published minimum age of 13, and private family tours are described for children from 9. The same waterfront building holds the kayak booking centre, a store and bookshop, and the Harbourview Coffeehouse.
venue.address: 320 Main Street, PO Box 620, Tofino, BC, V0R 2Z0

facility_notes.bus_parking: Downton Pay Parking is in effect every day from 9 AM - 6 PM until May 1 to October 31. The cost is $2.75hr for 6hrs max. There is also a municipal lot that allows full day and multiday parking on 3rd and Main parking.
facility_notes.rain_backup: We will not cancel bookings or offer refunds due to rain, clouds or fog.

restrictions: Group tour min age is 13yrs old and anyone under 16yrs must be in the front of a double kayak
Youth 9-15yrs old are required to be in the front of a double with an adult.
We require a minimum of 2 people for a tour to go.
Everyone in our booking can understand instructions in English without a translator.
Please read waiver prior to kayaking tour as you will be required to sign to take part in any of our activities.
You cannot be under influence of drugs or alcohol that could affect safety on the water.
Kayaks cockpits are able to fit people to approx. height of 6.4″ (195cm) and waist size of 46″(117cm)
Pregnant women can join tour in the first trimester up to 15 weeks only.
Sea kayaking is a physical activity. Including walking on uneven & slippery terrain. carrying kayaks, stairs, possible capsize, variety of weather conditions
venue.hours_notes: The kayak booking centre, retail store and bookstore are listed as open 8:30am to 5:00pm in September. The Harbourview Coffeehouse in the same building is listed as open Monday to Wednesday 8:30am to 4:00pm and Thursday to Sunday 8:30am to 5:00pm. No hours are published for any other month.
venue.seasonal_notes: Downtown Tofino pay parking runs every day from 9am to 6pm between May 1 and October 31, at $2.75 an hour for a maximum of six hours. A free town shuttle runs daily from June 27 to September 1.

programs.name: Harbour Islands day tour
programs.description: A 2.5 hour guided paddle around the islands in Tofino's harbour, published at $80 per person plus a 1% Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Park fee. The tours page describes it as designed for people new to kayaking or families, at an easy going pace with lots of instruction and stops. Morning and evening departures are mentioned but no exact start times are published. No experience is needed and all kayak gear, boots, a paddling jacket and dry bags are provided.
programs.what_children_do: Everyone starts on shore with an introductory lesson on how to paddle, how to steer and how to get out of the kayak if it tips. Then they paddle for about two and a half hours along the intertidal zones and waterways around the rainforest islands of the harbour, stopping along the way. Anyone under 16 rides in the front of a double kayak with an adult.
programs.our_note: Tours go ahead in rain, cloud and fog, and are only called off when the company judges the weather unsafe, so pack a full change of clothes for everyone including the adults. Feet get wet on purpose. One of their own listed reviews says a good part of the two and a half hours went on the shore briefing, so treat the paddling time as shorter than the tour length.
programs.practical_summary: Everything happens outdoors on the water, and nothing about washrooms, a place to eat or any indoor shelter appears anywhere on the site. Downtown parking is paid and capped at six hours with no word on where a bus would go, so call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: We collect a 1% Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Park fee to provide support for the traditional stewardship of Clayoquot Sound
programs.cancellation_note: Day Tours: Full payment is non-refundable within 48 hours of the tour start time. Cancellations prior to 48hours of tour start time payment is refundable.

programs.name: West Coaster day tour
programs.description: A 4 hour guided paddle out to the open coast, published at $128 per person plus a 1% Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Park fee. The page says no experience is necessary but that paddlers need to be prepared for moderate paddling time in varying conditions, with open crossings, currents, light winds and mild swell. The tour stops on shore for a snack break and there are several stops along the way to learn about the area.
programs.what_children_do: After the shore lesson on paddling, steering and what to do in a capsize, they paddle for about four hours along islands and across open channels, with a landing partway for a snack and a chance to stretch. Anyone under 16 rides in the front of a double kayak with an adult.
programs.our_note: This is the one with open crossings, swell and currents, so it asks a lot more of a teenager than the harbour paddle does. Bring a real lunch or a big snack, because nothing to eat is provided and four hours on the water builds an appetite.
programs.practical_summary: Four hours outdoors with one shore stop, and the site says nothing about washrooms, a place to eat or any indoor shelter. Paid downtown parking is capped at six hours, which is tight for this tour once you add gear and parking time, so ask about the longer stay lot when you call.

programs.name: Meares Big Tree Trail day tour
programs.description: A 4.5 hour guided trip to Meares Island, published at $144 per person plus a 1% Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Park fee. Paddlers cross to the island, land, and walk the rustic Big Tree Trail boardwalk among old growth cedars. Guides talk about the rainforest ecosystem and the history of the fight to protect the trees.
programs.what_children_do: They take the shore lesson, paddle along the shorelines of Meares Island, then land and walk the wild winding, rustic Big Tree Trail on a rough boardwalk among cedars that stand hundreds of feet tall, while the guide tells them how the trees came to be protected. Then they paddle back. Anyone under 16 rides in the front of a double kayak with an adult.
programs.our_note: This is the tour with a real walk in it, so footwear matters twice over. Feet get wet getting in and out of the kayak, and the boardwalk is rough and uneven, so bring dry socks and shoes that can handle both.
programs.practical_summary: Four and a half hours split between paddling and a forest walk, all of it outdoors. Washrooms, anywhere to eat and any shelter from the weather are not mentioned on the site, and bus parking is not addressed, so a phone call is worth it.

programs.name: Meares Hidden Places day tour
programs.description: A 5 hour guided paddle into Lemmens Inlet on Meares Island, published at $160 per person plus a 1% Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Park fee. The page describes exploring the eel grass ecosystem, the intertidal life and the bird habitat of the inlet. Guides stop to stretch legs, go for a walk in the forest and have a snack.
programs.what_children_do: After the shore lesson they paddle for most of five hours into the bays and inlets behind Meares Island, over eel grass flats and past intertidal life and birds, and get out partway for a short forest walk and a snack. Anyone under 16 rides in the front of a double kayak with an adult.
programs.our_note: Five hours is the longest thing they run as a day tour, and there is no way to cut it short once you are out there. Ask how much of that is actually on the water before you commit a group of teenagers to it.
programs.practical_summary: Five hours outdoors with one short landing, and the site does not mention washrooms, a lunch space or any shelter. Six hours is the most you can buy at a downtown parking meter, so ask about the longer stay lot when you call.

programs.name: Private family tour
programs.description: Any of the four day tours can be booked privately for one group, and the private family version is the only offering on the site that takes children under 13. Published private prices are $432 for up to 6 people and $864 for up to 12 on the 2.5 hour Harbour Island tour, $692 and $1384 on the 4 hour West Coaster, $778 and $1556 on the 4.5 hour Big Tree Trail, and $864 and $1728 on the 5 hour Hidden Places. The pricing table says 5% tax and a 1.5% Tribal Park fee are not included. Group sizing is one guide to six people, or two guides to twelve.
programs.what_children_do: They paddle in a double kayak with an adult, at a slower pace with more stops than the public tours, over kelp forests and along the shorelines, reaching out to grab kelp and things floating in the water and looking at the creatures on the tidal rocks. Much of the paddling ends up being done by the adult in the back.
programs.our_note: Every child under 16 has to share a double with an adult, so a group of nine year olds needs one adult per child, and that drives what you pay. On a private tour a guide can take a child if the adults do not divide evenly, which is not possible on a public tour, so say so when you call. Their own pages disagree about the upper age for a family tour, so settle it on the phone.
programs.practical_summary: The price is for the whole group rather than per child, and tax and the tribal park fee sit on top of it. Nothing about washrooms, a place to eat or shelter from the weather is published, and there is no word on bus parking, so ask about all of it when you book.
programs.cancellation_note: Private Tours: Full payment is non-refundable within 48 hours of the tour start time. Cancellations prior to 48hours of tours start time are charged Admin Fee: $60 upto 6people, 50% of tour cost over 6 people.

chaperone_ratio.applies_to: each child under 16, who must be paired with a parent in a double kayak

programs.evidence: Our private family tours are designed so kids from 9 to 12yrs old can participate and have fun getting out kayaking.

gaps: no school, daycare or youth group rate is published anywhere; the only group price is the private tour rate, which is the same whatever the group is
the site never mentions school groups, class bookings or educational programs, so whether it takes a school booking at all is unknown
the upper age for a private family tour is given as 12 on the family tours page and as 14 in the questions section on the same page, recorded as a conflict
the Tribal Park fee is given as 1% on all four day tour pages and as 1.5% in the private tour pricing table, recorded as a conflict
whether GST applies to the published day tour prices is not stated; only the private tour pricing table mentions tax
no start times are published for any tour; the harbour tour page mentions morning and evening departures but gives no clock times
which months tours run is unknown; the site publishes September opening hours for the booking centre and no season for the tours themselves
no minimum notice or lead time for booking is published; the tours page only says reservations are recommended
washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site
no indoor lunch space is described; the site says to bring snacks for shorter trips and a lunch for longer tours but does not say where a group could eat
no rain backup or indoor alternative is described; the site says it will not cancel or refund for rain, clouds or fog
bus parking is not addressed; the site describes downtown pay parking capped at six hours and a municipal lot on Third and Main
stroller and wheelchair access are not addressed; the site describes uneven and slippery terrain, carrying kayaks and stairs
the booking email address on the tour pages is hidden by the site's email protection script and cannot be read, so only the phone number and the online booking page are recorded
the four day tour pages were last updated in January 2025 and February 2025 and carry no price year or season, so the prices may be a season behind
the tour prices and availability are loaded by a booking widget that a plain fetch cannot run, so live dates and times were not visible
the image the site offers to social media is a Book Now button rather than a photograph, so the lead photo from the harbour tour page is used instead
the site's photos are lazy loaded and carry no real alt text, so four of the five alt lines were written here from the site's own captions and the page they sit on, without viewing the image files

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different top ages for a family tour, 12 in one place and 14 in another. Both agree the youngest is 9. Worth settling when you book if you have a 13 or 14 year old in the group.

There is a tribal park fee added on top of the tour price, and the site gives it as 1 percent in one place and 1.5 percent in another. It is small either way, but ask for the total when you book so the invoice matches.
